newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sea World Trust sees half yr profit fall.
newsitem.headline: Sea World Trust sees half yr profit fall.

text.p: Sea World Property Trust said on Friday that declines in attendances at its theme parks on Queensland'd Gold Coast would see a 10 percent to 15 percent drop in profitability for the six months ended June 30 this year.

Attendances at both Seaworld and Warner Bros Movie World parks on Queensland's Gold Coast were down due to a fall in international tourist numbers and weak levels of domestic tourism prevalent in the Australian economy, chairman Terry Jackman said in a statement.
"Coupled with the bad weather encountered over the main holiday period earlier in the year, the trust has been unable to claw back the shortfalls in rental income," Jackman said.
Despite the expected downturn in profitability, the trust saw no reason to be anything but confident about long-term and medium-term prospects, he said.
The company achieved a net profit of A$10.27 million in the first half of calendar 1996. It achieved a net profit of A$21.65 million in the full year.
